quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:

options.text: Turn the wheel too far in the opposite direction.
Turn your steering wheel toward traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction the back of the car is sliding.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction the back of the car is sliding.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle starts to skid, stay calm. Steer the wheel in the same direction the car is sliding.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid out of control, you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes quickly.
Press the brakes gently.
Do not use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle is skidding, do not use the brakes. Keep steering to regain control until the car is safe and moving normally again.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Drivers must let pedestrians cross safely in marked or unmarked crosswalks. For safety, always give pedestrians the right-of-way when they are crossing any street.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: These parking spaces are only for people with disabled parking permits.
A roundabout is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn the direction the arrow points.
This lane is for buses and vehicles carrying multiple passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are only for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that these parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: Drivers should watch carefully for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:

options.text: They are hard to see on the road.
They follow different traffic rules than cars.
They always have the right-of-way.
They do not have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see on the road.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers did not see motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians even though they were looking. These are smaller and harder to spot because they are less noticeable on the road. Always watch for these smaller road users.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep the same speed the whole time.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay close to the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Speed up gradually as you leave it. Speeding up when entering a curve makes your car harder to control.

questions.question: The correct way to use a freeway exit ramp is to:

options.text: Slow down before you enter the exit ramp.
Slow down after you enter the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the exit ramp.
Pass slower cars on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you enter the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until after you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.question: On the freeway, you see a merging traffic sign. You should:

options.text: Honk at the incoming cars.
Always keep the same speed.
Speed up to avoid slow traffic.
Change lanes if safe to let traffic merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes if safe to let traffic merge.
questions.explanation: On a road with two or more lanes, make space for vehicles entering. If the lane next to you is empty, move over.

questions.question: The law requires you to stay how far behind a snowplow with its red or amber lights on?

options.text: 200 feet
300 feet
400 feet
500 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 200 feet
questions.explanation: On roads with a speed limit of 35 mph or higher, you must stay at least 200 feet behind a working snowplow when its lights are on.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: When turning left on green, you must yield to oncoming traffic.
One-way street.
Cattle crossing ahead.
Two-way left turn lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning left on green, you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that when turning left on a green light, you must let oncoming traffic go first and only turn when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT safe for night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows make it harder to see in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: If you look into oncoming headlights, your eyes will narrow to protect themselves. After the car passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to normal. During this time, you cannot see the road clearly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for drunk drivers.
Curves ahead.
Slippery when wet.
Apply your brakes quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: When backing up, you should drive no faster than:

options.text: A slow crawl.
A slow walk.
A jog.
A sprint.

questions.correctAnswerText: A slow walk.
questions.explanation: When driving in reverse, go no faster than a slow walk. It is much harder to control a vehicle when moving backwards.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then cross when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, you should:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels straight.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking on a downhill slope, turn your wheels toward the side of the road. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: Round signs warn drivers about:

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Upcoming railroad crossings.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you of an upcoming railroad crossing. Use extra caution when you see this sign.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane with the broken line.
You can pass from the lane with the solid line.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: Regulatory signs:

options.text: Are placed everywhere there is danger.
Tell you what you must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
Warn you about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell you what you must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black text on a white background. They tell you what you must or must not do, such as speed limits or turning restrictions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead is red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead is green.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a traffic signal is coming at the next intersection ahead.

questions.question: If an oncoming vehicle uses high beams, you should look toward ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle's high beams are on and not dimmed, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When parking your vehicle on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Touch one of your rear wheels to the curb.
Use your parking brake and put the vehicle in "park."
Turn your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and put the vehicle in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and put the vehicle in "park" when parking on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your front wheels so the car rolls away from the road center if brakes fail. If there is a curb, turn wheels toward it when heading downhill, or away from it when heading uphill.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to do when driving through a curve?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's momentum can make it hard to turn. To stay in control, you must slow down before entering the curve.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side of the road means you can cross it to pass other vehicles when the road is clear.

questions.question: When does your vehicle need more distance to stop?

options.text: On a wet or icy road.
On paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Your stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on roads with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: A car suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk your horn and brake hard.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a car cuts in front of you, release the gas pedal. This creates space between you and the other car without requiring you to brake hard or swerve.

questions.question: You are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Finish crossing the intersection, then pull right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, then pull right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or siren, finish crossing the intersection. Then drive to the right and stop. You must yield to all emergency vehicles using flashing lights or sirens.

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane early, but do not slow down until after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to follow specific instructions are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs give orders that drivers must follow. Breaking these rules can result in a penalty.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain because oil in the asphalt rises to the surface. This is worse in hot weather, when heat causes more oil to reach the road surface.

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning in rainy conditions?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit like you would in good weather.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions and your tires lose contact with the road. The car rides on top of the water. The best way to prevent this is to drive slower in rain than in dry conditions.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beam headlights in fog or mist?

options.text: The light reflects back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles cannot see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light reflects back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights reflect the light back toward you. This makes it harder to see the road.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street, where should you drive?

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: Start in the lane closest to the centerline. Begin your turn just before you reach the center of the intersection. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: How far ahead should you signal before turning?

options.text: 25 feet
50 feet
75 feet
100 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Signal 100 feet before you turn. However, wait to signal if there are other streets or driveways between you and your turn. Signal only when your turn is the next move.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: A no passing zone.
A one-way traffic area.
The blind spot around a large vehicle.
An area for motor vehicles only.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot around a large vehicle.
questions.explanation: A "No zone" is a blind spot around large trucks and vehicles. Avoid staying in these areas.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so other drivers let you through.
Drive around the rear of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting. This way, if another vehicle hits you from behind, you will not be pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: You want to turn left. To whom should you give the right-of-way?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles also turning left.
All approaching vehicles.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting to walk.

questions.correctAnswerText: All approaching vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all other vehicles moving on their green light.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to construction.
The road ahead makes a sharp turn at a steep angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead makes a sharp turn at a steep angle.
questions.explanation: This warning sign tells you to slow down. The road ahead will turn at a very sharp angle.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid dangerous driving situations?

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always focus your eyes straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Be aware of what is happening around your vehicle at all times. Watch the front, sides, and rear. This helps you spot problems and decide if you need to change speed or position.

questions.question: An oncoming driver has high beams on. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you see enough to stay on course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Begin slowing down.
Flash your headlights.
Honk your horn loudly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn loudly.
questions.explanation: Honk your horn loudly when a child or pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: You are driving in the left lane with two lanes going your direction. Many cars are passing you on the right. The driver behind you wants to go faster. You should:

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Drive onto the left shoulder.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane for passing or turning left. Use the right lane when going slower than other traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always have the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only when convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, but an approaching vehicle may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: When you get in a car to drive, what should you adjust first?

options.text: Your seat belt
The steering wheel
Your rearview mirror
Your seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat first to sit comfortably and see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel based on your seat position.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, you should:

options.text: Stop immediately.
Drive to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
Drive slowly and let it pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle is coming, drive as far right as you safely can and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Leave the front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb or parking downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb.

questions.question: When you arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles to your right and left, you should:

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until there are no other vehicles before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: If another driver is passing you in a no passing zone, you should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down to help the passing vehicle safely return to the lane and avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: If your vehicle's rear is skidding to the left, you should:

options.text: Not turn the steering wheel.
Turn the steering wheel to the left.
Turn the steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, take your foot off the gas, do not brake, and turn the wheel in the direction of the skid. If you have anti-lock brakes, apply them firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
Slow down and proceed carefully.
Stop completely and stay stopped until the light changes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
